plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.9
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the double integral of (2x - y^2) over the triangular region R enclosed between y = -x + 1, y = x + 1, and y = 3. The figure shows the triangular region R in the xy-plane with vertices at (-2, 3), (0, 1), and (2, 3); the bounding lines y = 3 (top), y = -x + 1 (lower left), and y = x + 1 (lower right) are labeled. The y-axis divides R into two sub-regions: R1 (shaded blue, left half) and R2 (shaded yellow, right half), each with a red vertical strip indicating the direction of inner integration. The figure illustrates the decomposition of R into two type-I sub-regions required when the lower boundary changes expression across the y-axis.

interactionPlan.concept: A vertically sliced double integral over this triangular region must be split into two Type-I integrals because the lower boundary is y = -x + 1 on the left of the y-axis and y = x + 1 on the right.

interactions.label: Lower boundary equations
interactions.teaches: The two inner limits are different because the lower edge of the region is described by one formula for -2 ≤ x ≤ 0 and by another formula for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2

demo_steps.title: See the split at the y-axis
demo_steps.narration: The same triangular region is sliced vertically, so each slice runs from a lower boundary up to y = 3. Because the lower boundary changes formula at x = 0, the region is divided into R1 and R2.

demo_steps.title: Connect each boundary to its integral limits
demo_steps.narration: The left shaded region uses y = -x + 1 as its lower limit, while the right shaded region uses y = x + 1. The displayed integral limits update directly from the two boundary equations.

demo_steps.title: Edit a lower boundary
demo_steps.narration: Change either lower-boundary equation and watch that side of the region redraw. The corresponding lower limit in the double integral changes with it, showing why each sub-region needs its own integral.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A Type-I decomposition is needed whenever vertical slices encounter different lower-boundary formulas on different x-intervals.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a clean xy-plane with the triangular region above the x-axis, apex at (0,1), and top base from approximately x = -2 to x = 2 at y = 3. Use a thick cyan-blue outline for all three triangle edges. Shade the left half light blue and label it R1; shade the right half pale yellow and label it R2. Place the y-axis through the apex and the midpoint of the top edge, visibly dividing the triangle into two sub-regions. Add one red vertical slice in each half, extending from the corresponding lower boundary to the top line y = 3. Keep the top boundary fixed at y = 3 while the two editable lower boundaries redraw over their respective domains. Show the updated integral limits beside or below the diagram as two summed iterated integrals.
